newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-ZAGALLO STILL UNDER FIRE, DESPITE COPA WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZAGALLO STILL UNDER FIRE, DESPITE COPA WIN.

text.p: Brazil's 3-1 win over Bolivia in the final of the Copa America was hailed in the country's press on Monday but manager Mario Zagallo still came in for criticism.
"We're going to have to tolerate Zagallo," read a headline in the newspaper Correio Braziliense.
The veteran coach lost no time after Sunday's game in attacking his critics who have questioned whether he should be in charge of Brazil in next year's World Cup finals in France.
"I love Brazil, others hate it...Now you're going to have to put up with me," he yelled at television reporters before running on to the pitch to congratulate his players.

Newspaper columnists were quick to comment on Zagallo's outburst. "Phrases (like that), made with a hot head, do not match with his career, his experience and much less with his white hairs," wrote Fernando Calazans in daily O Globo.
But most of the media prefered to focus on the team's achievement in overcoming Bolivia in front of a fervent home crowd in La Paz and the difficulties of playing at 3,600 metres above sea level.

Brazil had previously won the Copa America four times but never on foreign soil. Roberto Benavides, writing in O Estado de Sao Paulo, said Zagallo's team had pulled off what previous sides, some of which included legendary players Pele and Garrincha, failed to do.
